questions.question: _______ remained the mainstay of the Green Revolution for years in India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Wheat**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Green Revolution was an endeavour initiated by Norman Borlaug in the 1960s.
 
• He is known as the 'Father of Green Revolution' in world.'
 
• In India, the Green Revolution was mainly led by M.S. Swaminathan.
 
• The Green Revolution resulted in a great increase in the production of food grains (especially wheat and rice) due to the introduction into developing countries of new, high-yielding variety seeds, beginning in the mid-20th century.
 
• The Green Revolution in India is largely the Wheat Revolution as the wheat production increased by more than three times between 1967-68 and 2003-04, while the overall increase in the production of cereals was only two times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Important Crops in the Revolution:

 
 
• The main crops were Wheat, Rice, Jowar, Bajra and Maize.
 
• Non-food grains were excluded from the ambit of the new strategy.
 
• Wheat remained the mainstay of the Green Revolution for years.

questions.question: Which type of expenditure refers to expenses that do not lead to the creation of physical or financial assets?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Revenue Expenditure**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The type of expenditure that refers to expenses that do not lead to the creation of physical or financial assets is ** Revenue Expenditure**.
 
• These are expenses incurred for the day-to-day functioning of the government, such as salaries, maintenance, and other operational costs. 
 
• They do not result in the creation of long-term assets.
 
• Revenue expenditures are typically **recurring expenses**.
 
• **Examples**:
 
 
• **Salaries and Wages**
 
 
• Payments made to government employees and workers.
 
 
 
• **Maintenance Costs**
 
 
• Expenses for the upkeep of existing infrastructure, such as roads, schools, and hospitals.
 
 
 
• **Subsidies and Grants**
 
 
• Financial assistance provided to various sectors or communities to support economic activity and welfare.
 
 
 
• **Interest Payments**
 
 
• Payments made on government debt.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure**

 
 
• This refers to expenditures that lead to the creation of physical or financial assets, such as infrastructure projects or purchasing machinery.
 
 
 
• **Development Expenditure**
 
 
• This includes spending aimed at enhancing the economic capacity and social welfare of the country, which can involve both capital and revenue expenditures.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Expenditure**
 
 
• This term broadly refers to all government spending, encompassing both revenue and capital expenditures.

questions.question: The Green Revolution significantly increased crop yields and transformed Indian agriculture. What was one of its notable drawbacks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Environmental degradation**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• One of the notable drawbacks of the **Green Revolution** was **Environmental degradation**
 
• Environmental degradation consist of Soil Degradation,Water Depletion,Chemical Pollution
 
• The heavy use of **pesticides and herbicides** to protect the high-yielding crops from pests and weeds contributed to environmental pollution.
 
• The Green Revolution promoted the use of **irrigation-intensive crops**, particularly wheat and rice, which required large amounts of water
 
 
• This led to over-extraction of groundwater, especially in regions like Punjab and Haryana
 
 
 
• The excessive use of **chemical fertilizers** (such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium-based fertilizers) gradually degraded soil quality. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Green Revolution** 

 
 
• The **Green Revolution** refers to a period during the 1960s and 1970s when India significantly increased its agricultural production.
 
• The introduction of **high-yielding varieties (HYVs)** of seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and improved irrigation techniques. 
 
• his movement was initiated to address India's food security concerns and prevent famines.
 
• The Green Revolution focused on increasing access to irrigation
 
 
• through the construction of canals, dams, and tubewells to ensure adequate water supply for agriculture.

questions.question: Right to property is a ________ under the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitutional Right**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to Property is a **Constitutional legal Right.**
 
• Originally, the **Right to Property was a Fundamental Right under Article 31 **of the Indian Constitution when it was adopted in 1950. 
 
• This article **provided protection against deprivation of property** without compensation.
 
• In **1976**, during the Emergency period, the **42nd Amendment** to the Constitution redefined the status of the Right to Property
 
• It was removed from the list of Fundamental Rights and was made a Legal Right
 
• The **Right to Property as a Constitutional Right ensures **that individuals have a legal claim to their property
 
• It provides a framework for the protection of property rights in India.
 
• While it c**annot be enforced as a Fundamental Right, it still holds constitutional validity.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Rights**

 
 
• **Fundamental Rights are explicitly mentioned in Part III** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring their legal protection
 
• Fundamental Rights are enforceable by the courts, allowing individuals to seek l**egal recourse if their rights are violated.**
 
• **There are 6 Fundamental Rights .**
 
 
 
• **Directive Principle**
 
 
• **​Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines enshrined in Part IV of the Constitution **of India that are intended to guide the government in policy-making and governance.
 
• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles are not enforceable by the courts. However, **they are essential for framing laws and policies.**
 
• They aim to promote social and economic welfare, ensuring that citizens receive a fair share of the country’s resources.
 
 
 
• **Non Constitutional Right-**
 
 
• **​**Unlike Constitutional Rights (such as Fundamental Rights), Non-Constitutional Rights do not have a dedicated section in the constitution.

questions.question: How many horizontal rows are present in the modern periodic table?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**7**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The modern periodic table has **7 horizontal rows**, which are called **periods**.
 
• Each **period corresponds to the number of electron shells** an atom of an element in that row.
 
• The** 7 periods in the periodic table** represent the number of electron shells in an element's atom.
 
• The elements in each period have increasing atomic numbers as you move from left to right, and their properties change accordingly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **modern periodic table** is a tabular arrangement of all known chemical elements, organized based on their atomic numbers, electron configurations, and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Elements are arranged in increasing order of their **atomic number** (the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom).
 
• There are **18 groups** in the periodic table.
 
• Elements in the same group have the same number of valence electrons, which gives them similar chemical properties.
 
• The table is divided into **s-block**, **p-block**, **d-block**, and **f-block** based on the type of atomic orbitals the electrons occupy.
